newsitem.title: UK: "Eurosceptics" ad for Beck's beer found misleading.
newsitem.headline: "Eurosceptics" ad for Beck's beer found misleading.

text.p: A British advertising trade group on Wednesday said it upheld a complaint that a "Eurosceptics" advertisement for Beck's beer was misleading.
The Advertising and Standards Authority (ASA) said it received complaints from the European Commission, the European Movement and a European Parliament member over the newspaper ad for Beck's beer.
The ad showed a picture of of Brussels sprouts arranged in a circle and the headline, "Keep them out of our BIER."

The ad continued: "Things used to be so simple. ... But now we have Brussels. Well-meaning chaps but perhaps a little zealous? ... They're even looking at the merits of standardising the way we brew our bier.

"Imagine this. Your are teasing yourself with an ice cold Beck's ... You anticipate the melange of Hallertau hops and yeast combined with the purest glacial water ... you succumb to temptation. But your tastebuds tell you something is wrong. Your Beck's is not your Beck's. And do you know why? Because in their infinite wisdom Brussels has decreed that all bier must now be brewed with an inferior 'standardised' water."
The ad was created by the Barker & Ralston agency for Scottish Courage, the unit of drinks and leisure company Scottish and Newcastle Plc which produces Beck's.
The ASA said the advertisers maintained the ad was humorous and was not misleading because the European Commission was considering a proposal that could affect the water with which Beck's was brewed.

"But the Authority noted that the advertisers had not shown that the proposal as drafted would affect Beck's" the ASA said. "It considered that the advertisers had distorted the present position and it concluded that the advertisement was misleading," the ASA said.
The ASA noted that the first version of the ad has been amended, and it said the revised ad, and the rest of the ad campaign, "were more clearly humorous and unlikely to mislead."
In other complaints received, the ASA said it upheld an objection to an on-pack promotion for Bass Brewers' Worthington Draught Bitter that enclosed a free special edition of Loaded magazine.
The on-pack promotion for the magazine showed comedian Harry Enfield dressed as a woman, saying, "My boys love to get Loaded, especially when it's free."
Complainants objected to the contents of the magazine, including quotes from famous people using sexually explicit language, as offensive and obscene.
The ASA said the edition of the magazine was likley to offend many people, and it asked the advertisers to put a warning on the packaging or on the front of the promotional issue.

The ASA did not uphold a complaint against an ad in Gay Times magazine that featured various bondage items above the words "gagged", "bound", "whipped" and "restrained." The ad also read, "No, this isn't an ad for Amnesty... eather and rubber clothes, toys and twisted gear. Who says safe sex can't be great sex?"
Although the complainant said the ad was offensive and drew on the torture of gay people, the ASA ruled it was unlikely to cause serious or widespread offence to the magazine's readers.

The ASA did uphold a complaint against a leaflet advertising skateboarding equipment for Rollersnakes Ltd that showed a photograph of two men, one bloodied, lying face up on the ground and holding a gun. The other man in the photo was shown with a manic grin standing over the first and holding a chain-saw to his neck.
The ASA said the photo was likely to cause widespread or serious offence. The advertisers said they had already withdrawn the leaflet after complaints from parents.
